purpose: Balanced feature-set guidance for keeping enough signal to avoid underfitting without leaning too hard into narrow metric-specific winners.

criteria.must_keep: Appears in at least 3 of the 4 best-overall metric winners.
criteria.maybe_keep: Appears in exactly 2 best-overall metric winners, or appears in 1 best-overall metric winner but still shows strong support across per-method best entries.
criteria.probably_drop: Appears in only 1 best-overall metric winner and has limited support across per-method best entries.

must_keep.reason: Foundational pre-race signal that shows up in every best-overall objective and every per-method best winner.
The other core starting-position feature; just as stable as grid across all objectives and methods.
Recurring cross-objective driver-strength signal that helps both winner picking and full-order quality.
Shows up repeatedly as a stable team-trend feature without being tied to only one metric.
Strong recurring team-identity signal across multiple objectives, though it still deserves monitoring for shift risk.

maybe_keep.reason: Useful for front-of-field race outcomes, but not stable enough across every objective to be automatic.
Strong support for order-quality metrics and repeatedly useful in per-method winners.
Helpful circuit-history signal, but more objective-specific than the core features.
Consistent circuit-context feature, especially for outcome-focused metrics.
Stable team-strength signal for ordering metrics, with solid support across method-specific winners.
Useful when tyre strategy matters, but less universal than the main performance signals.
Contextual race-condition feature that can help, but likely depends on limited event patterns.
Potentially useful environmental context, but more situational than the stable competitive signals.
Helps capture circuit identity, though it can also increase memorization risk if overused.
Mostly winner-focused, but recurring enough in per-method best entries to keep in the discussion.
More useful for broad position quality than for winner picking, but supported often enough to avoid a hard drop.

probably_drop.reason: Looks helpful for a narrow winner-focused objective, but shows limited cross-objective and cross-method stability.
Only shows up for one best-overall objective and has limited support elsewhere.

notes: These buckets are for building a balanced general-purpose feature set, not for maximizing a single metric at all costs.
A feature in probably_drop is not useless; it just has the weakest evidence for broad, stable generalization in the current search output.
If you later build metric-specific models, features like quali_gap or circuit_overperformance may deserve promotion for winner-only optimization.
